title: Catalogue presents no level-one heading
summary: The product catalogue at /#/search contains no level-one heading at all. The highest-ranked heading in the document is an h2 carrying the site brand in the toolbar, so no heading names the page. A screen-reader user navigating by heading level has nothing that identifies where they are. Confirmed by a requirement-traced test that is recorded as a strict expected failure, so fixing the application will surface here rather than silently passing.

evidence.requirement: JS-CAT-2 - The catalogue page shall expose exactly one level-one heading naming the page
evidence.highest_heading_present: h2: 'OWASP Juice Shop' (toolbar brand, not a page name)
evidence.measurement_state: welcome banner and cookie banner dismissed, catalogue fully rendered (15 product cards present)
evidence.verifying_test_output: AssertionError: expected one level-one heading, found []
evidence.test_status: xfail(strict=True) - tracked open finding, not a silenced failure
evidence.system_under_test: OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0, locally hosted
evidence.detected_by: accessibility facet during role-scoped discovery, corrected after manual verification
evidence.correction_note: An earlier revision of this finding recorded three level-one headings, naming 'Welcome to OWASP Juice Shop!' and 'https://owasp-juice.shop'. That was wrong. Both of those headings belong to the first-visit welcome banner, which is a modal dialog rendered above the page, and neither is page content. The catalogue itself has none. The error came from the accessibility facet, whose missing-h1 check used document.querySelector('h1') and so counted the dialog's headings as the page's - it therefore reported no defect on a page that has no heading at all. The detector now scopes document-outline checks to page content, excluding dialog subtrees, and records modal_dialog_open as context when a dialog covers the page.
